# Line reflections and the orthogonal group

## Abstract

In a finite-dimensional real inner product space the reflections in lines generate the whole orthogonal group when the dimension is even and exactly the isometries of determinant one when the dimension is odd.

**Theorem 1.1 (The subgroup generated by line reflections).**

$$\forall F \in \operatorname{Type}*,\; [\operatorname{NormedAddCommGroup}\left(F\right)] [\operatorname{InnerProductSpace}\left(\mathbb{R}, F\right)] [\operatorname{FiniteDimensional}\left(\mathbb{R}, F\right)] \forall g \in \operatorname{LinearIsometryEquiv}\left(\mathbb{R}, F, F\right),\; g \in \operatorname{closure}\left(\{r \in \operatorname{LinearIsometryEquiv}\left(\mathbb{R}, F, F\right) \mid \exists v \in F,\; v \ne 0 \land r = \operatorname{reflection}\left(\operatorname{span}\left(\mathbb{R}, \left\{v\right\}\right)\right)\}\right) \Leftrightarrow \left(\operatorname{Even}\left(\operatorname{finrank}\left(\mathbb{R}, F\right)\right) \lor \operatorname{det}\left(g\right) = 1\right)$$

*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Quantum/Algebra/Comparison/LineReflectionGeneration.mem_closure_lineReflections_iff` (`✓ std3`). ∎

*Source.* Repository-derived.

*Commentary.*

Let F be a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension n, and for a nonzero vector v let the line reflection be the orthogonal reflection in the line span(R, {v}): it fixes v and acts as minus the identity on the orthogonal complement of v. In the display, LinearIsometryEquiv(R, F, F) is the group of linear isometries of F onto itself, closure(S) is the subgroup generated by a set S of isometries, r is the generic element of the generating set, finrank(R, F) = n is the dimension, and det(g) is the determinant of the underlying linear map of g. The statement is: an isometry g is a finite product of line reflections and their inverses if and only if n is even or det(g) = 1. Thus the line reflections generate the whole orthogonal group in even dimension and exactly the isometries of determinant one in odd dimension. The dimensions zero and one are included; in dimension one every line reflection is the identity, and in dimension zero the group is trivial.

The reflection in the hyperplane orthogonal to a nonzero vector v is minus the line reflection in span(R, {v}), and it has determinant -1. By the Cartan-Dieudonne theorem every isometry g is a product of k hyperplane reflections, so g = (-1)^k h with h a product of k line reflections and det(g) = (-1)^k. If det(g) = 1 then k is even and g = h lies in the generated subgroup. In even dimension the isometry -1 is the reflection in the zero subspace and has determinant (-1)^n = 1, so it lies in the generated subgroup, and therefore so does every g = (-1)^k h. In odd dimension the orthogonal complement of a line has even dimension n - 1, so every line reflection has determinant (-1)^(n-1) = 1; the determinant is multiplicative, hence every element of the generated subgroup has determinant one.

Both conditions are needed. The hypothesis v nonzero matters, because the reflection in the zero line is -1, which would make every isometry a product of generators in every dimension. The parity of the dimension cannot be dropped: in odd dimension the isometry -1 has determinant -1 and is not a product of line reflections. The generation of the orthogonal group by hyperplane reflections is the classical Cartan-Dieudonne theorem; the parity refinement for line reflections is a standard consequence of it.
